sentences.text: Massaliasuchus is an extinct genus of allodaposuchid eusuchian crocodyliform found in the Late Cretaceous Fuvelian Lignites of southeastern France.
Massaliasuchus was first described in 1869 by Philippe Matheron based on skull bones originally named Crocodilus affuvelensis.
The genus Massaliasuchus was renamed in 2008 by Jeremy Martin and Eric Buffetaut.
Massaliasuchus can be distinguished from Musturzabalsuchus by having 15 alveoli in the dentary bone.
Massaliasuchus is often omitted from phylogenetic analyses because it is known only from poorly preserved material.
Recent analysis classifies Massaliasuchus as a member of Allodaposuchidae, a group of basal eusuchians from the Late Cretaceous of southern Europe.
Massaliasuchus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
